title: Wikipedia: Another Brick in the Wall
content: Another Brick in the Wall is a three-part Pink Floyd composition from The Wall, released in 1979. Roger Waters wrote the song. Part 2 is associated with a children's choir, protest themes about oppressive schooling, and a disco-influenced production approach. The single topped the US Billboard Hot 100 and UK singles chart. title: Wikipedia: Stars on 45 Medley
content: Stars on 45 was a Dutch pop act directed by producer Jaap Eggermont and known for medleys that recreated familiar songs over a common tempo and drum track. The Stars on 45 Medley was released in the early 1980s, reached number one in the United States, and was followed by the Long Play Album. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: Everybody Wants to Rule the World
content: Everybody Wants to Rule the World is a Tears for Fears song from Songs from the Big Chair, released in 1985. It was written by Roland Orzabal, Ian Stanley, and Chris Hughes and produced by Hughes. The new wave and synth-pop song addresses the desire for power and the effects of warfare. It reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: Walk of Life
content: Walk of Life is a Dire Straits song from Brothers in Arms, released as a single in the United States in 1985 and the United Kingdom in 1986. Mark Knopfler wrote the song. Its arrangement combines rock and roll with a synthesizer-led keyboard riff and blues and zydeco influences. It reached number seven in the United States and number two in the United Kingdom. title: Wikipedia: Another Day in Paradise
content: Another Day in Paradise is a Phil Collins song from ...But Seriously, released as a single in 1989. Collins wrote and produced the soft rock song with Hugh Padgham. Its subject is homelessness and the discomfort of ignoring people in need. The song became Collins' seventh solo US Billboard Hot 100 number one and the last US number one of the 1980s.
